## Description

A smaller paramecium (~130 × 40 µm) with the same way of life as *P. caudatum*. In Gause's (1934)
mixed culture it displaces *P. caudatum*: competitive exclusion. It is sensitive to the R bodies of
killer paramecia (*P. tetraurelia*): it eats them with the bacteria and dies within hours.

## In the simulation

<!-- GENERATED:presence -->
Drops: `pond` (weight 0.15), `puddle` (weight 0.15); 20 individuals in a reference drop at weight 1.
<!-- /GENERATED -->

Like *P. caudatum*, with its ingestion and clearance scaled allometrically from it
(V^0.75 and V^0.77) and [sensitivity to the killer signal](../../mechanics/chemical-signals.md#signal-toxicity-killer-paramecium)
(dose estimated). Gause monoculture plateau validated.

## Literature

- Gause G.F. (1934), fig. 22 (own logistic fit: r = 0.707 ± 0.090/day, K = 222; temperature not
  verified).
- Hansen P.J., Bjørnsen P.K., Hansen B.W. (1997) Zooplankton grazing and growth: scaling within the 2–2,000-µm body size range. Limnol. Oceanogr. 42: 687–704.
- Sonneborn T.M. (1938) (killer trait).

## Not implemented yet

- No measured feeding data of its own.
- Gause's exclusion result is not reproduced for the right reason ([bug](../../bugs/gause-aurelia-does-not-win.md)).
- Helix radius and period are estimates (of the order of Bullington 1925 and Jennings 1906).
- Trichocysts are a defence gene, not discharged organelles that can be counted.
- Contractile vacuole period in fresh water estimated; cytosol osmolarity taken from *P. caudatum*.

## Unique and shared mechanics

Competes with *P. caudatum* in the [well-mixed culture](../../mechanics/well-mixed-culture.md); the sensitive
partner of *P. tetraurelia*.
